## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Changes are needed before merge. Removing the defaults file breaks its existing loader; the new helpers also reject a valid port and hide configuration failures.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Deleting this file makes every call to `load_defaults()` at `app/startup.py:6` raise `FileNotFoundError`. Restore the file or update the loader to obtain defaults elsewhere. — Existing callers can no longer load default configuration.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — For port `65535`, `0 < p < 65535` returns false despite the documented inclusive range. Change the upper comparison to `<= 65535`. — A valid TCP port is rejected.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — For a missing file or malformed JSON, `except Exception` discards the underlying error and returns `{}` without a signal or documented fallback behavior. Propagate the error or explicitly document and expose the fallback. — Callers cannot distinguish broken configuration from a successfully loaded empty configuration.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — The trailing-dot branch for `"Example.COM."` has no coverage; the existing host test only exercises lowercasing. Add an assertion that this input produces `"example.com"`. — A regression that stops removing trailing dots would pass the current tests.
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring promises “returns None when h is empty,” but the empty-input branch executes `return ""`. Align the documented return value with the intended behavior. — Callers following the documentation receive a different empty-input result.

## Strengths
- The millisecond timeout test checks the converted value: `"1500ms"` produces `1.5`.
- The configuration success test checks the parsed contents of a temporary JSON file.
